functions.name: ERREXIT
functions.signature: Macro: ERREXIT(cinfo, code)
functions.description: Reports a fatal JPEG error. Sets the error manager’s msg_code to code and immediately calls the error handler via err->error_exit((j_common_ptr)cinfo). Intended for unrecoverable conditions; control is not expected to return to the caller.
requirements: cinfo must point to a valid libjpeg common/compress/decompress structure (convertible to j_common_ptr).
cinfo->err must be non-NULL and initialized (for example via jpeg_std_error or equivalent custom error manager).
cinfo->err->error_exit must be a valid function pointer; it is expected not to return (commonly longjmp/exit).
code must be a valid J_MESSAGE_CODE (J_MESSAGE_CODE enum value).
Do not pass expressions with side effects for cinfo, as the macro references (cinfo) multiple times.

functions.name: ERREXIT1
functions.signature: Macro: ERREXIT1(cinfo, code, p1)
functions.description: Reports a fatal JPEG error with one integer parameter. Sets msg_code and msg_parm.i[0] = p1, then calls err->error_exit((j_common_ptr)cinfo). Use when a single integer argument is needed for the formatted message.
requirements: All ERREXIT requirements apply.
p1 must be representable as int (stored in msg_parm.i[0]).

functions.name: ERREXIT2
functions.signature: Macro: ERREXIT2(cinfo, code, p1, p2)
functions.description: Reports a fatal JPEG error with two integer parameters. Sets msg_code and msg_parm.i[0..1], then calls error_exit.
requirements: All ERREXIT requirements apply.
p1 and p2 must be representable as int (stored in msg_parm.i[0], msg_parm.i[1]).

functions.name: ERREXIT3
functions.signature: Macro: ERREXIT3(cinfo, code, p1, p2, p3)
functions.description: Reports a fatal JPEG error with three integer parameters. Sets msg_code and msg_parm.i[0..2], then calls error_exit.
requirements: All ERREXIT requirements apply.
p1, p2, p3 must be representable as int (stored in msg_parm.i[0..2]).

functions.name: ERREXIT4
functions.signature: Macro: ERREXIT4(cinfo, code, p1, p2, p3, p4)
functions.description: Reports a fatal JPEG error with four integer parameters. Sets msg_code and msg_parm.i[0..3], then calls error_exit.
requirements: All ERREXIT requirements apply.
p1, p2, p3, p4 must be representable as int (stored in msg_parm.i[0..3]).

functions.name: ERREXIT6
functions.signature: Macro: ERREXIT6(cinfo, code, p1, p2, p3, p4, p5, p6)
functions.description: Reports a fatal JPEG error with six integer parameters. Sets msg_code and msg_parm.i[0..5], then calls error_exit.
requirements: All ERREXIT requirements apply.
p1..p6 must be representable as int (stored in msg_parm.i[0..5]).

functions.name: ERREXITS
functions.signature: Macro: ERREXITS(cinfo, code, str)
functions.description: Reports a fatal JPEG error with a string parameter. Sets msg_code and copies str into err->msg_parm.s using strncpy with capacity JMSG_STR_PARM_MAX, explicitly NUL-terminating, then calls error_exit.
requirements: All ERREXIT requirements apply.
str must be a valid pointer to a NUL-terminated character sequence. It will be truncated to JMSG_STR_PARM_MAX-1 bytes if longer.
JMSG_STR_PARM_MAX must be defined appropriately by the libjpeg headers included before use (normally provided by the library).

functions.name: WARNMS
functions.signature: Macro: WARNMS(cinfo, code)
functions.description: Emits a nonfatal warning message. Sets err->msg_code to code and calls err->emit_message((j_common_ptr)cinfo, -1). Execution continues after the call.
requirements: cinfo must point to a valid libjpeg structure with an initialized error manager (cinfo->err).
cinfo->err->emit_message must be a valid function pointer.
code must be a valid J_MESSAGE_CODE.
Do not pass expressions with side effects for cinfo (used multiple times).

functions.name: WARNMS1
functions.signature: Macro: WARNMS1(cinfo, code, p1)
functions.description: Emits a nonfatal warning message with one integer parameter. Sets msg_code and msg_parm.i[0] = p1, then calls emit_message with level -1.
requirements: All WARNMS requirements apply.
p1 must be representable as int (stored in msg_parm.i[0]).

functions.name: WARNMS2

functions.description: Emits a nonfatal warning message with two integer parameters. Sets msg_code and msg_parm.i[0..1], then calls emit_message with level -1.
requirements: All WARNMS requirements apply.
p1 and p2 must be representable as int (stored in msg_parm.i[0..1]).

functions.name: TRACEMS
functions.signature: Macro: TRACEMS(cinfo, lvl, code)
functions.description: Emits an informational/debug trace message at the given verbosity level. Sets msg_code to code and calls err->emit_message((j_common_ptr)cinfo, lvl).
requirements: cinfo must point to a valid libjpeg structure with an initialized error manager (cinfo->err).
cinfo->err->emit_message must be a valid function pointer.
code must be a valid J_MESSAGE_CODE.
lvl is an integer trace level; emission depends on the error manager’s configured trace level.
Do not pass expressions with side effects for cinfo (used multiple times).

functions.name: TRACEMS1
functions.signature: Macro: TRACEMS1(cinfo, lvl, code, p1)
functions.description: Emits a trace message with one integer parameter. Sets msg_code and msg_parm.i[0] = p1, then calls emit_message with the specified level.
requirements: All TRACEMS requirements apply.
p1 must be representable as int (stored in msg_parm.i[0]).

functions.name: TRACEMS2
functions.signature: Macro: TRACEMS2(cinfo, lvl, code, p1, p2)
functions.description: Emits a trace message with two integer parameters. Sets msg_code and msg_parm.i[0..1], then calls emit_message with the specified level.
requirements: All TRACEMS requirements apply.
p1 and p2 must be representable as int (stored in msg_parm.i[0..1]).

functions.name: TRACEMS3
functions.signature: Macro: TRACEMS3(cinfo, lvl, code, p1, p2, p3)
functions.description: Emits a trace message with three integer parameters. Stores p1..p3 into msg_parm.i[0..2], sets msg_code, and calls emit_message at the specified level. Implemented via a compound statement to ensure single evaluation of p1..p3, but cinfo is still referenced multiple times.
requirements: All TRACEMS requirements apply.
p1, p2, p3 must be representable as int (stored in msg_parm.i[0..2]).

functions.name: TRACEMS4
functions.signature: Macro: TRACEMS4(cinfo, lvl, code, p1, p2, p3, p4)
functions.description: Emits a trace message with four integer parameters. Stores p1..p4 into msg_parm.i[0..3], sets msg_code, and calls emit_message at the specified level.
requirements: All TRACEMS requirements apply.
p1, p2, p3, p4 must be representable as int (stored in msg_parm.i[0..3]).

functions.name: TRACEMS5
functions.signature: Macro: TRACEMS5(cinfo, lvl, code, p1, p2, p3, p4, p5)
functions.description: Emits a trace message with five integer parameters. Stores p1..p5 into msg_parm.i[0..4], sets msg_code, and calls emit_message at the specified level.
requirements: All TRACEMS requirements apply.
p1..p5 must be representable as int (stored in msg_parm.i[0..4]).

functions.name: TRACEMS8
functions.signature: Macro: TRACEMS8(cinfo, lvl, code, p1, p2, p3, p4, p5, p6, p7, p8)
functions.description: Emits a trace message with eight integer parameters. Stores p1..p8 into msg_parm.i[0..7], sets msg_code, and calls emit_message at the specified level.
requirements: All TRACEMS requirements apply.
p1..p8 must be representable as int (stored in msg_parm.i[0..7]).

functions.name: TRACEMSS
functions.signature: Macro: TRACEMSS(cinfo, lvl, code, str)
functions.description: Emits a trace message with a string parameter. Sets msg_code, copies str into err->msg_parm.s using strncpy with capacity JMSG_STR_PARM_MAX and ensures NUL termination, then calls emit_message with the specified level.
requirements: All TRACEMS requirements apply.
str must be a valid pointer to a NUL-terminated character sequence. It will be truncated to JMSG_STR_PARM_MAX-1 bytes if longer.
JMSG_STR_PARM_MAX must be defined appropriately by the libjpeg headers included before use (normally provided by the library).

functions.name: jpeg_std_error
functions.signature: struct jpeg_error_mgr *jpeg_std_error(struct jpeg_error_mgr *err);
functions.description: Initializes a jpeg_error_mgr with default libjpeg error-handling callbacks and returns the same pointer. Typical first step before creating a JPEG object.
requirements: err must be a non-NULL pointer to writable storage for struct jpeg_error_mgr
Must be called before jpeg_create_compress() or jpeg_create_decompress() to install an error manager

functions.name: jpeg_create_compress
functions.signature: void jpeg_create_compress(j_compress_ptr cinfo);
functions.description: Macro wrapper that initializes a compressor object. Expands to jpeg_CreateCompress(cinfo, JPEG_LIB_VERSION, sizeof(struct jpeg_compress_struct)).
requirements: cinfo must be non-NULL and point to writable storage at least sizeof(struct jpeg_compress_struct)
An error manager must be set (cinfo->err) prior to calling (see jpeg_std_error)
Caller must have included system headers defining FILE and size_t before jpeglib.h (global requirement from header comments)

functions.name: jpeg_create_decompress
functions.signature: void jpeg_create_decompress(j_decompress_ptr cinfo);
functions.description: Macro wrapper that initializes a decompressor object. Expands to jpeg_CreateDecompress(cinfo, JPEG_LIB_VERSION, sizeof(struct jpeg_decompress_struct)).
requirements: cinfo must be non-NULL and point to writable storage at least sizeof(struct jpeg_decompress_struct)
An error manager must be set (cinfo->err) prior to calling (see jpeg_std_error)
Caller must have included system headers defining FILE and size_t before jpeglib.h (global requirement from header comments)

functions.name: jpeg_CreateCompress
functions.signature: void jpeg_CreateCompress(j_compress_ptr cinfo, int version, size_t structsize);
functions.description: Initializes a JPEG compression object with version/size checks. Called by jpeg_create_compress macro.
requirements: cinfo must be non-NULL and point to storage at least structsize bytes
cinfo->err must be initialized (e.g., via jpeg_std_error) before calling
version should match JPEG_LIB_VERSION; mismatch triggers error handling
structsize should be sizeof(struct jpeg_compress_struct)

functions.name: jpeg_CreateDecompress
functions.signature: void jpeg_CreateDecompress(j_decompress_ptr cinfo, int version, size_t structsize);
functions.description: Initializes a JPEG decompression object with version/size checks. Called by jpeg_create_decompress macro.
requirements: cinfo must be non-NULL and point to storage at least structsize bytes
cinfo->err must be initialized (e.g., via jpeg_std_error) before calling
version should match JPEG_LIB_VERSION; mismatch triggers error handling
structsize should be sizeof(struct jpeg_decompress_struct)

functions.name: jpeg_destroy_compress
functions.signature: void jpeg_destroy_compress(j_compress_ptr cinfo);
functions.description: Destroys a compressor object and releases all associated resources.
requirements: cinfo must point to an initialized compressor object created by jpeg_create_compress/jpeg_CreateCompress
After call, the object must not be used unless reinitialized

functions.name: jpeg_destroy_decompress
functions.signature: void jpeg_destroy_decompress(j_decompress_ptr cinfo);
functions.description: Destroys a decompressor object and releases all associated resources.
requirements: cinfo must point to an initialized decompressor object created by jpeg_create_decompress/jpeg_CreateDecompress
After call, the object must not be used unless reinitialized

functions.name: jpeg_stdio_dest
functions.signature: void jpeg_stdio_dest(j_compress_ptr cinfo, FILE *outfile);
functions.description: Sets the compression data destination to a stdio FILE for writing JPEG output.
requirements: cinfo must be a valid, initialized compressor
outfile must be an open FILE* for writing; caller is responsible for opening/closing the file
Must be called before jpeg_start_compress()

functions.name: jpeg_stdio_src
functions.signature: void jpeg_stdio_src(j_decompress_ptr cinfo, FILE *infile);
functions.description: Sets the decompression data source to a stdio FILE for reading JPEG input.
requirements: cinfo must be a valid, initialized decompressor
infile must be an open FILE* for reading; caller is responsible for opening/closing the file
Must be called before jpeg_read_header()

functions.name: jpeg_mem_dest
functions.signature: void jpeg_mem_dest(j_compress_ptr cinfo, unsigned char **outbuffer, unsigned long *outsize);
functions.description: Sets the compression data destination to a dynamically-managed memory buffer. On completion, *outbuffer points to the JPEG data and *outsize to its size.
requirements: cinfo must be a valid, initialized compressor
outbuffer and outsize must be non-NULL pointers to variables; the function writes to them
Must be called before jpeg_start_compress()
Ownership/allocator of the returned buffer is not specified in this header; refer to library docs for deallocation requirements (unknown here)

functions.name: jpeg_mem_src
functions.signature: void jpeg_mem_src(j_decompress_ptr cinfo, const unsigned char *inbuffer, unsigned long insize);
functions.description: Sets the decompression data source to a memory buffer containing a complete JPEG datastream.
requirements: cinfo must be a valid, initialized decompressor
inbuffer must be non-NULL and point to insize bytes of JPEG data
insize is the size in bytes of inbuffer
Must be called before jpeg_read_header()

functions.name: jpeg_set_defaults
functions.signature: void jpeg_set_defaults(j_compress_ptr cinfo);
functions.description: Initializes compression parameters in cinfo to reasonable defaults based on in_color_space and other fields.
requirements: cinfo must be a valid, initialized compressor
cinfo->in_color_space must be set correctly before calling
image dimensions and input_components should be set by the application before starting compression

functions.name: jpeg_set_colorspace
functions.signature: void jpeg_set_colorspace(j_compress_ptr cinfo, J_COLOR_SPACE colorspace);
functions.description: Sets the target JPEG colorspace and updates component parameters accordingly.
requirements: cinfo must be a valid, initialized compressor
Should be called after jpeg_set_defaults() and before jpeg_start_compress()

functions.name: jpeg_default_colorspace
functions.signature: void jpeg_default_colorspace(j_compress_ptr cinfo);
functions.description: Sets a default JPEG colorspace based on the input colorspace.
requirements: cinfo must be a valid, initialized compressor
Should be called after jpeg_set_defaults() and before jpeg_start_compress()

functions.name: jpeg_set_quality
functions.signature: void jpeg_set_quality(j_compress_ptr cinfo, int quality, boolean force_baseline);
functions.description: Sets quantization tables based on a quality factor (typically 0–100).
requirements: cinfo must be a valid, initialized compressor
Should be called after jpeg_set_defaults() and before jpeg_start_compress()
quality is an application-provided integer; valid range not specified in header (common convention is 0..100; exact behavior for out-of-range is unspecified here)

functions.name: jpeg_set_linear_quality
functions.signature: void jpeg_set_linear_quality(j_compress_ptr cinfo, int scale_factor, boolean force_baseline);
functions.description: Sets quantization tables using a linear scaling factor rather than perceived-quality mapping.
requirements: cinfo must be a valid, initialized compressor
Should be called after jpeg_set_defaults() and before jpeg_start_compress()
scale_factor is an application-provided integer; valid range not specified in header

functions.name: jpeg_default_qtables
functions.signature: void jpeg_default_qtables(j_compress_ptr cinfo, boolean force_baseline);
functions.description: (JPEG_LIB_VERSION >= 70) Initializes default quantization tables in the compressor object.
requirements: cinfo must be a valid, initialized compressor
Available only when JPEG_LIB_VERSION >= 70
Should be called before jpeg_start_compress()

functions.name: jpeg_add_quant_table
functions.signature: void jpeg_add_quant_table(j_compress_ptr cinfo, int which_tbl, const unsigned int *basic_table, int scale_factor, boolean force_baseline);
functions.description: Defines or updates a quantization table in the compressor from a baseline table scaled by scale_factor.
requirements: cinfo must be a valid, initialized compressor
which_tbl must be in range 0..3 (NUM_QUANT_TBLS-1)
basic_table must be a valid pointer to 64-entry table data (assumed by context; exact size not stated here)
Should be called before jpeg_start_compress()

functions.name: jpeg_quality_scaling
functions.signature: int jpeg_quality_scaling(int quality);
functions.description: Maps a quality factor to an internal scaling factor used for quantization tables.
requirements: quality is an application-provided integer; valid range not specified in header

functions.name: jpeg_enable_lossless
functions.signature: void jpeg_enable_lossless(j_compress_ptr cinfo, int predictor_selection_value, int point_transform);
functions.description: Configures the compressor for lossless JPEG encoding with the given predictor and point transform.
requirements: cinfo must be a valid, initialized compressor
Should be called before jpeg_start_compress()
predictor_selection_value and point_transform are integers; valid ranges are not specified in this header

functions.name: jpeg_simple_progression
functions.signature: void jpeg_simple_progression(j_compress_ptr cinfo);
functions.description: Configures a standard multi-scan progressive encoding script in the compressor.
requirements: cinfo must be a valid, initialized compressor
Should be called before jpeg_start_compress()

functions.name: jpeg_suppress_tables
functions.signature: void jpeg_suppress_tables(j_compress_ptr cinfo, boolean suppress);
functions.description: Controls whether quantization/Huffman tables are emitted into the output stream.
requirements: cinfo must be a valid, initialized compressor
Call before or during compression setup as appropriate; see library docs (details not in header)

functions.name: jpeg_alloc_quant_table
functions.signature: JQUANT_TBL *jpeg_alloc_quant_table(j_common_ptr cinfo);
functions.description: Allocates a quantization table object from the JPEG memory manager.
requirements: cinfo must be a valid JPEG object (compressor or decompressor) with memory manager initialized
Never returns NULL; on failure, error_exit is invoked (per header’s memory manager notes)

functions.name: jpeg_alloc_huff_table
functions.signature: JHUFF_TBL *jpeg_alloc_huff_table(j_common_ptr cinfo);
functions.description: Allocates a Huffman table object from the JPEG memory manager.
requirements: cinfo must be a valid JPEG object (compressor or decompressor) with memory manager initialized
Never returns NULL; on failure, error_exit is invoked

functions.name: jpeg_start_compress
functions.signature: void jpeg_start_compress(j_compress_ptr cinfo, boolean write_all_tables);
functions.description: Starts JPEG compression. Computes derived parameters and writes headers (optionally writing all tables).
requirements: cinfo must be a valid, initialized compressor with input image fields and parameters set
Destination manager (e.g., jpeg_stdio_dest or jpeg_mem_dest) must be configured
Must be called before jpeg_write_scanlines()/jpeg_write_raw_data()

functions.name: jpeg_write_scanlines
functions.signature: JDIMENSION jpeg_write_scanlines(j_compress_ptr cinfo, JSAMPARRAY scanlines, JDIMENSION num_lines);
functions.description: Feeds one or more rows of interleaved sample data to the compressor in lossy mode. Returns the number of lines actually written.
requirements: cinfo must be in compression state after jpeg_start_compress()
scanlines must point to at least num_lines rows, each with cinfo->input_components samples per pixel
Row width must match cinfo->image_width
num_lines >= 0
Use the 12/16-bit variants when data_precision is 12 or 16

functions.name: jpeg12_write_scanlines
functions.signature: JDIMENSION jpeg12_write_scanlines(j_compress_ptr cinfo, J12SAMPARRAY scanlines, JDIMENSION num_lines);
functions.description: Feeds 9–12-bit sample rows to the compressor. Returns the number of lines actually written.
requirements: cinfo must be in compression state after jpeg_start_compress()
Use when data_precision is 9..12; scanlines element type is J12SAMPLE
Buffer dimensions must match image width and components
num_lines >= 0

functions.name: jpeg16_write_scanlines
functions.signature: JDIMENSION jpeg16_write_scanlines(j_compress_ptr cinfo, J16SAMPARRAY scanlines, JDIMENSION num_lines);
functions.description: Feeds 13–16-bit sample rows to the compressor. Returns the number of lines actually written.
requirements: cinfo must be in compression state after jpeg_start_compress()
Use when data_precision is 13..16; scanlines element type is J16SAMPLE
Buffer dimensions must match image width and components
num_lines >= 0

functions.name: jpeg_finish_compress
functions.signature: void jpeg_finish_compress(j_compress_ptr cinfo);
functions.description: Finishes JPEG compression, writes EOI, and flushes destination.
requirements: cinfo must be a compressor in an active compression sequence started by jpeg_start_compress()
After return, no more data can be written unless reinitialized

functions.name: jpeg_calc_jpeg_dimensions
functions.signature: void jpeg_calc_jpeg_dimensions(j_compress_ptr cinfo);
functions.description: (JPEG_LIB_VERSION >= 70) Precalculates the JPEG output dimensions (cinfo->jpeg_width/height) for current compression parameters without starting compression.
requirements: cinfo must be a valid, initialized compressor
Available only when JPEG_LIB_VERSION >= 70

functions.name: jpeg_write_raw_data
functions.signature: JDIMENSION jpeg_write_raw_data(j_compress_ptr cinfo, JSAMPIMAGE data, JDIMENSION num_lines);
functions.description: Supplies downsampled component-plane data directly to the compressor instead of interleaved scanlines. Returns the number of lines actually consumed.
requirements: cinfo must be in compression state after jpeg_start_compress() and configured for raw_data_in = TRUE
data must reference per-component sample planes with dimensions matching downsampled sizes
num_lines must be a positive multiple appropriate to the iMCU height (exact multiple not specified here)

functions.name: jpeg12_write_raw_data
functions.signature: JDIMENSION jpeg12_write_raw_data(j_compress_ptr cinfo, J12SAMPIMAGE data, JDIMENSION num_lines);
functions.description: 12-bit variant of jpeg_write_raw_data for supplying downsampled component-plane data. Returns the number of lines consumed.
requirements: cinfo must be in compression state after jpeg_start_compress() and configured for raw_data_in = TRUE
Use when data_precision is 9..12
data must reference per-component planes sized to downsampled dimensions
num_lines must be a positive multiple appropriate to the iMCU height (unspecified here)

functions.name: jpeg_write_marker
functions.signature: void jpeg_write_marker(j_compress_ptr cinfo, int marker, const JOCTET *dataptr, unsigned int datalen);
functions.description: Writes a JPEG marker (COM or APPn, etc.) with the provided data to the output stream. See libjpeg.txt for safe usage.
requirements: cinfo must be a compressor in a valid state for writing markers (typically after jpeg_start_compress() and before EOI)
marker must be a valid marker code (e.g., JPEG_COM, JPEG_APP0+n)
dataptr may be NULL only if datalen is zero; otherwise must point to at least datalen bytes
datalen is the number of data bytes to write (marker length word is handled internally)

functions.name: jpeg_write_m_header
functions.signature: void jpeg_write_m_header(j_compress_ptr cinfo, int marker, unsigned int datalen);
functions.description: Begins writing a marker segment by emitting the marker and length; data bytes should be supplied subsequently via jpeg_write_m_byte.
requirements: cinfo must be a compressor in a valid state for writing markers
marker must be a valid marker code
datalen specifies the number of data bytes to follow

functions.name: jpeg_write_m_byte
functions.signature: void jpeg_write_m_byte(j_compress_ptr cinfo, int val);
functions.description: Writes a single data byte as part of a marker segment started with jpeg_write_m_header.
requirements: cinfo must be a compressor in a valid state within a marker write sequence
val must be in 0..255 (stored in a byte)

functions.name: jpeg_write_tables
functions.signature: void jpeg_write_tables(j_compress_ptr cinfo);
functions.description: Writes an abbreviated JPEG stream containing only the tables currently defined in the compressor object.
requirements: cinfo must be a valid, initialized compressor
Destination manager must be set
Typically called without writing image data; see library docs for sequence

functions.name: jpeg_write_icc_profile
functions.signature: void jpeg_write_icc_profile(j_compress_ptr cinfo, const JOCTET *icc_data_ptr, unsigned int icc_data_len);
functions.description: Embeds an ICC color profile in the JPEG output via APP2 markers.
requirements: cinfo must be a compressor in a valid state for writing markers
icc_data_ptr must point to icc_data_len bytes of ICC profile data (may be split internally)
icc_data_len specifies profile size

functions.name: jpeg_read_header
functions.signature: int jpeg_read_header(j_decompress_ptr cinfo, boolean require_image);
functions.description: Reads the beginning of the JPEG datastream and parses headers (SOI, tables, SOF, etc.). Returns status indicating header completeness.
requirements: cinfo must be a valid, initialized decompressor with a source manager set (e.g., jpeg_stdio_src or jpeg_mem_src)
require_image = TRUE will cause an error for tables-only streams; when FALSE, JPEG_HEADER_TABLES_ONLY may be returned
May return JPEG_SUSPENDED if the source supports suspension

functions.name: jpeg_start_decompress
functions.signature: boolean jpeg_start_decompress(j_decompress_ptr cinfo);
functions.description: Starts the decompression process and computes output dimensions/parameters. Returns TRUE on success/readiness for output.
requirements: cinfo must be a valid decompressor after successful jpeg_read_header()
Output parameters (e.g., out_color_space, scaling) should be set before calling

functions.name: jpeg_read_scanlines
functions.signature: JDIMENSION jpeg_read_scanlines(j_decompress_ptr cinfo, JSAMPARRAY scanlines, JDIMENSION max_lines);
functions.description: Reads one or more output scanlines of decompressed samples into the caller-provided buffer. Returns the number of lines actually read.
requirements: cinfo must be in decompression output state after jpeg_start_decompress()
scanlines must point to storage for at least max_lines rows of width cinfo->output_width and components cinfo->output_components
max_lines >= 0

functions.name: jpeg12_read_scanlines
functions.signature: JDIMENSION jpeg12_read_scanlines(j_decompress_ptr cinfo, J12SAMPARRAY scanlines, JDIMENSION max_lines);
functions.description: Reads 9–12-bit output scanlines into a 12-bit sample buffer. Returns the number of lines actually read.
requirements: cinfo must be in decompression output state after jpeg_start_decompress()
Use when data_precision is 9..12
Buffer width must match cinfo->output_width and components cinfo->output_components
max_lines >= 0

functions.name: jpeg16_read_scanlines
functions.signature: JDIMENSION jpeg16_read_scanlines(j_decompress_ptr cinfo, J16SAMPARRAY scanlines, JDIMENSION max_lines);
functions.description: Reads 13–16-bit output scanlines into a 16-bit sample buffer. Returns the number of lines actually read.
requirements: cinfo must be in decompression output state after jpeg_start_decompress()
Use when data_precision is 13..16
Buffer width must match cinfo->output_width and components cinfo->output_components
max_lines >= 0

functions.name: jpeg_skip_scanlines
functions.signature: JDIMENSION jpeg_skip_scanlines(j_decompress_ptr cinfo, JDIMENSION num_lines);
functions.description: Skips over a number of output scanlines without returning them to the application, returning the number actually skipped.
requirements: cinfo must be in decompression output state after jpeg_start_decompress()
num_lines >= 0

functions.name: jpeg12_skip_scanlines
functions.signature: JDIMENSION jpeg12_skip_scanlines(j_decompress_ptr cinfo, JDIMENSION num_lines);
functions.description: 12-bit variant of jpeg_skip_scanlines.
requirements: cinfo must be in decompression output state after jpeg_start_decompress()
Use when data_precision is 9..12
num_lines >= 0

functions.name: jpeg_crop_scanline
functions.signature: void jpeg_crop_scanline(j_decompress_ptr cinfo, JDIMENSION *xoffset, JDIMENSION *width);
functions.description: Adjusts the output scanline window by cropping: sets an x offset and width for subsequent scanline reads.
requirements: cinfo must be a valid decompressor; typical use is after jpeg_read_header() and before/while output is configured
xoffset and width must be non-NULL pointers; function reads/writes through them
Exact constraints on cropping values are not detailed in header

functions.name: jpeg12_crop_scanline
functions.signature: void jpeg12_crop_scanline(j_decompress_ptr cinfo, JDIMENSION *xoffset, JDIMENSION *width);
functions.description: 12-bit variant of jpeg_crop_scanline.
requirements: cinfo must be a valid decompressor
xoffset and width must be non-NULL pointers
Exact constraints on cropping values are not detailed in header

functions.name: jpeg_finish_decompress
functions.signature: boolean jpeg_finish_decompress(j_decompress_ptr cinfo);
functions.description: Finishes the decompression process, ensuring all input is consumed and output is finalized. Returns TRUE on success.
requirements: cinfo must be a decompressor that has started decompression via jpeg_start_decompress()

functions.name: jpeg_read_raw_data
functions.signature: JDIMENSION jpeg_read_raw_data(j_decompress_ptr cinfo, JSAMPIMAGE data, JDIMENSION max_lines);
functions.description: Reads raw downsampled component-plane data from the decompressor. Returns the number of lines actually read.
requirements: cinfo must be in decompression state configured for raw_data_out = TRUE
data must reference per-component buffers sized to downsampled output dimensions
max_lines must be a positive multiple appropriate to the iMCU height (unspecified here)

functions.name: jpeg12_read_raw_data
functions.signature: JDIMENSION jpeg12_read_raw_data(j_decompress_ptr cinfo, J12SAMPIMAGE data, JDIMENSION max_lines);
functions.description: 12-bit variant of jpeg_read_raw_data for downsampled component-plane data. Returns the number of lines read.
requirements: cinfo must be in decompression state configured for raw_data_out = TRUE
Use when data_precision is 9..12
data must reference per-component buffers sized to downsampled output dimensions
max_lines must be a suitable multiple for iMCU height (unspecified here)

functions.name: jpeg_has_multiple_scans
functions.signature: boolean jpeg_has_multiple_scans(j_decompress_ptr cinfo);
functions.description: Indicates whether the JPEG file contains multiple scans (e.g., progressive or multi-scan sequential).
requirements: cinfo must be a valid decompressor after jpeg_read_header()

functions.name: jpeg_start_output
functions.signature: boolean jpeg_start_output(j_decompress_ptr cinfo, int scan_number);
functions.description: Begins output of a particular scan in buffered-image mode.
requirements: cinfo must be configured for buffered_image = TRUE and have input available
scan_number identifies the scan to output; valid range depends on the image; not specified in header

functions.name: jpeg_finish_output
functions.signature: boolean jpeg_finish_output(j_decompress_ptr cinfo);
functions.description: Finishes output of the current scan in buffered-image mode.
requirements: cinfo must be in buffered-image mode and have started a scan via jpeg_start_output()

functions.name: jpeg_input_complete
functions.signature: boolean jpeg_input_complete(j_decompress_ptr cinfo);
functions.description: Returns whether the entire JPEG datastream has been consumed by the input side of the decompressor.
requirements: cinfo must be a valid decompressor

functions.name: jpeg_new_colormap
functions.signature: void jpeg_new_colormap(j_decompress_ptr cinfo);
functions.description: Signals that the application supplied a new colormap for quantized output (buffered-image mode).
requirements: cinfo must be a valid decompressor
Meaningful only when quantize_colors is TRUE and buffered_image mode is used

functions.name: jpeg_consume_input
functions.signature: int jpeg_consume_input(j_decompress_ptr cinfo);
functions.description: Advances the input side of the decompressor, parsing more data. Returns a status code such as JPEG_REACHED_SOS/EOI, JPEG_ROW_COMPLETED, etc.
requirements: cinfo must be a valid decompressor with a source manager installed
May return JPEG_SUSPENDED if the source supports suspension

functions.name: jpeg_core_output_dimensions
functions.signature: void jpeg_core_output_dimensions(j_decompress_ptr cinfo);
functions.description: (JPEG_LIB_VERSION >= 80) Computes core output dimensions that do not depend on color quantization or other optional passes.
requirements: cinfo must be a valid decompressor
Available only when JPEG_LIB_VERSION >= 80

functions.name: jpeg_calc_output_dimensions
functions.signature: void jpeg_calc_output_dimensions(j_decompress_ptr cinfo);
functions.description: Computes output dimensions based on current decompression parameters (scaling, IDCT, etc.).
requirements: cinfo must be a valid decompressor (typically after jpeg_read_header())

functions.name: jpeg_save_markers
functions.signature: void jpeg_save_markers(j_decompress_ptr cinfo, int marker_code, unsigned int length_limit);
functions.description: Configures the decompressor to save APPn/COM markers of a given type into cinfo->marker_list up to a given size.
requirements: cinfo must be a valid decompressor
marker_code must be JPEG_COM or JPEG_APP0+n
length_limit is the maximum number of data bytes to save per marker

functions.name: jpeg_set_marker_processor
functions.signature: void jpeg_set_marker_processor(j_decompress_ptr cinfo, int marker_code, jpeg_marker_parser_method routine);
functions.description: Installs a custom parser callback for a specific marker code during decompression.
requirements: cinfo must be a valid decompressor
marker_code must be a marker value (e.g., JPEG_COM or JPEG_APP0+n)
routine may be NULL to remove a custom processor or must match signature boolean (*)(j_decompress_ptr)

functions.name: jpeg_read_coefficients
functions.signature: jvirt_barray_ptr *jpeg_read_coefficients(j_decompress_ptr cinfo);
functions.description: Reads the DCT coefficient arrays from the JPEG bitstream for potential transcoding without full decompression.
requirements: cinfo must be a valid decompressor after jpeg_read_header()
Returns a pointer to virtual block arrays; lifetime managed by the JPEG object

functions.name: jpeg_write_coefficients
functions.signature: void jpeg_write_coefficients(j_compress_ptr cinfo, jvirt_barray_ptr *coef_arrays);
functions.description: Writes a JPEG image using caller-supplied DCT coefficient arrays (for transcoding).
requirements: cinfo must be a valid compressor with destination set
coef_arrays must be the coefficient arrays to write, typically obtained from jpeg_read_coefficients()
Call before finishing compression; sequence details not specified in header

functions.name: jpeg_copy_critical_parameters
functions.signature: void jpeg_copy_critical_parameters(j_decompress_ptr srcinfo, j_compress_ptr dstinfo);
functions.description: Copies critical JPEG parameters from a decompressor to a compressor to allow lossless transcoding of coefficients.
requirements: srcinfo must be a valid decompressor after jpeg_read_header()
dstinfo must be a valid, initialized compressor
Call before jpeg_write_coefficients()

functions.name: jpeg_abort_compress
functions.signature: void jpeg_abort_compress(j_compress_ptr cinfo);
functions.description: Aborts an in-progress compression operation, releasing working memory so the object can be reused.
requirements: cinfo must be a valid compressor object (in any state)

functions.name: jpeg_abort_decompress
functions.signature: void jpeg_abort_decompress(j_decompress_ptr cinfo);
functions.description: Aborts an in-progress decompression operation, releasing working memory so the object can be reused.
requirements: cinfo must be a valid decompressor object (in any state)

functions.name: jpeg_abort
functions.signature: void jpeg_abort(j_common_ptr cinfo);
functions.description: Generic abort for either compressor or decompressor, releasing working memory so the object can be reused.
requirements: cinfo must be a valid JPEG object (compressor or decompressor)

functions.name: jpeg_destroy
functions.signature: void jpeg_destroy(j_common_ptr cinfo);
functions.description: Generic destroy for either compressor or decompressor object, releasing all resources.
requirements: cinfo must be a valid JPEG object (compressor or decompressor) created by jpeg_create_*

functions.name: jpeg_resync_to_restart
functions.signature: boolean jpeg_resync_to_restart(j_decompress_ptr cinfo, int desired);
functions.description: Default restart-marker resynchronization procedure used by data source modules on decompression errors.
requirements: cinfo must be a valid decompressor
desired is the desired restart interval index; exact valid range not specified in header

functions.name: jpeg_read_icc_profile
functions.signature: boolean jpeg_read_icc_profile(j_decompress_ptr cinfo, JOCTET **icc_data_ptr, unsigned int *icc_data_len);
functions.description: Extracts an embedded ICC profile from the JPEG datastream if present, allocating a buffer and returning it and its length.
requirements: cinfo must be a valid decompressor after jpeg_read_header() (and typically after reading markers)
icc_data_ptr and icc_data_len must be non-NULL pointers to receive outputs
On success, *icc_data_ptr will point to allocated data; allocation/ownership details not specified in header

functions.name: tj3Init
functions.signature: DLLEXPORT tjhandle tj3Init(int initType);
functions.description: Create a new TurboJPEG instance for compression, decompression, or lossless transform based on initType.
requirements: initType must be one of TJINIT_COMPRESS, TJINIT_DECOMPRESS, or TJINIT_TRANSFORM
On failure returns NULL; retrieve error with tj3GetErrorStr(NULL or handle)

functions.name: tj3Destroy
functions.signature: DLLEXPORT void tj3Destroy(tjhandle handle);
functions.description: Destroy a TurboJPEG instance. No effect if handle is NULL.
requirements: handle may be NULL (no-op)
After destroying, the handle must not be used again

functions.name: tj3GetErrorStr
functions.signature: DLLEXPORT char *tj3GetErrorStr(tjhandle handle);
functions.description: Return a descriptive error message for the last command associated with handle (or global function if handle is NULL; thread-safety of that is platform-dependent).
requirements: If called for a global function error, pass handle = NULL (thread-safe only if platform supports TLS)
Returned pointer is managed by library (no free implied; lifetime unspecified)

functions.name: tj3GetErrorCode
functions.signature: DLLEXPORT int tj3GetErrorCode(tjhandle handle);
functions.description: Return severity code of the last error for the given handle (TJERR_WARNING or TJERR_FATAL).
requirements: handle must be a valid TurboJPEG instance

functions.name: tj3Set
functions.signature: DLLEXPORT int tj3Set(tjhandle handle, int param, int value);
functions.description: Set a TurboJPEG parameter on the instance. See TJPARAM documentation for each parameter’s valid values/semantics.
requirements: handle must be a valid TurboJPEG instance
param must be one of TJPARAM values; value must respect the documented range/semantics for that param
Returns 0 on success, -1 on error (check tj3GetErrorStr/Code)

functions.name: tj3Get
functions.signature: DLLEXPORT int tj3Get(tjhandle handle, int param);
functions.description: Get the current value of a TurboJPEG parameter on the instance.
requirements: handle must be a valid TurboJPEG instance
param must be one of TJPARAM values
Returns -1 if value is unknown

functions.name: tj3Alloc
functions.signature: DLLEXPORT void *tj3Alloc(size_t bytes);
functions.description: Allocate a byte buffer for use with TurboJPEG (typically JPEG destination buffers).
requirements: bytes is the number of bytes to allocate; must be within addressable memory limits
Returned pointer should be freed with tj3Free()

functions.name: tj3Free
functions.signature: DLLEXPORT void tj3Free(void *buffer);
functions.description: Free a byte buffer previously allocated by TurboJPEG (tj3Alloc or auto-(re)allocated JPEG buffers).
requirements: buffer may be NULL (no-op)
Only pass pointers allocated by TurboJPEG

functions.name: tj3JPEGBufSize
functions.signature: DLLEXPORT size_t tj3JPEGBufSize(int width, int height, int jpegSubsamp);
functions.description: Return the maximum buffer size (bytes) required to hold a JPEG image with given dimensions and subsampling (TJSAMP).
requirements: width and height must be positive and within library limits
jpegSubsamp should be one of TJSAMP values; TJSAMP_UNKNOWN is treated as TJSAMP_444
Returns 0 if arguments are out of bounds

functions.name: tj3YUVBufSize
functions.signature: DLLEXPORT size_t tj3YUVBufSize(int width, int align, int height, int subsamp);
functions.description: Return the size (bytes) required for a unified planar YUV image with given dimensions, row alignment, and subsampling.
requirements: width and height must be positive
align must be a power of 2 (1 = unpadded)
subsamp must be one of TJSAMP values
Returns 0 if arguments are out of bounds

functions.name: tj3YUVPlaneSize
functions.signature: DLLEXPORT size_t tj3YUVPlaneSize(int componentID, int width, int stride, int height, int subsamp);
functions.description: Return the size (bytes) required for a single YUV image plane for given image dimensions, stride, and subsampling.
requirements: componentID must be 0 (Y), 1 (U/Cb), or 2 (V/Cr)
width and height refer to whole image dimensions and must be positive
stride 0 means use plane width; otherwise must be >= plane width
subsamp must be one of TJSAMP values
Returns 0 if arguments are out of bounds

functions.name: tj3YUVPlaneWidth
functions.signature: DLLEXPORT int tj3YUVPlaneWidth(int componentID, int width, int subsamp);
functions.description: Return the plane width (in samples) for a given YUV component with the specified image width and subsampling.
requirements: componentID must be 0, 1, or 2
width must be positive
subsamp must be one of TJSAMP values
Returns 0 if arguments are out of bounds

functions.name: tj3YUVPlaneHeight
functions.signature: DLLEXPORT int tj3YUVPlaneHeight(int componentID, int height, int subsamp);
functions.description: Return the plane height (in samples) for a given YUV component with the specified image height and subsampling.
requirements: componentID must be 0, 1, or 2
height must be positive
subsamp must be one of TJSAMP values
Returns 0 if arguments are out of bounds

functions.name: tj3SetICCProfile
functions.signature: DLLEXPORT int tj3SetICCProfile(tjhandle handle, unsigned char *iccBuf, size_t iccSize);
functions.description: Associate an ICC color profile with the instance for embedding into subsequently generated JPEG images (compression or lossless transform). Passing NULL or size 0 removes any previously associated profile.
requirements: handle must be initialized for compression or transform
iccBuf points to ICC profile data; a copy is made, so caller may free/modify after return
If iccBuf is NULL or iccSize is 0, any existing profile association is removed
Returns 0 on success, -1 on error

functions.name: tj3Compress8
functions.signature: DLLEXPORT int tj3Compress8(tjhandle handle, const unsigned char *srcBuf, int width, int pitch, int height, int pixelFormat, unsigned char **jpegBuf, size_t *jpegSize);
functions.description: Compress an 8-bit-per-sample packed-pixel RGB/Gray/CMYK image into a JPEG image with the same data precision.
requirements: handle must be initialized for compression
srcBuf must point to a valid source buffer sized at least pitch*height samples (or a region)
width,height must be positive
pitch 0 implies width * tjPixelSize[pixelFormat]; otherwise must be >= that for unpadded images or sized appropriately for regions
pixelFormat must be a valid TJPF value
jpegBuf must be a valid pointer to a pointer; library may allocate/realloc unless TJPARAM_NOREALLOC is set
If pre-allocating, *jpegSize must contain buffer size; upon return *jpegSize is set to actual JPEG size
Set parameters like TJPARAM_QUALITY, TJPARAM_SUBSAMP, etc., as needed prior to call
Returns 0 on success, -1 on error

functions.name: tj3Compress12
functions.signature: DLLEXPORT int tj3Compress12(tjhandle handle, const short *srcBuf, int width, int pitch, int height, int pixelFormat, unsigned char **jpegBuf, size_t *jpegSize);
functions.description: Compress a 9–12-bit-per-sample packed-pixel RGB/Gray/CMYK image into a JPEG image with the same data precision.
requirements: Same structural requirements as tj3Compress8, but srcBuf is short* and precision set via TJPARAM_PRECISION (defaults to 12 if unset/out of range)
Returns 0 on success, -1 on error

functions.name: tj3Compress16
functions.signature: DLLEXPORT int tj3Compress16(tjhandle handle, const unsigned short *srcBuf, int width, int pitch, int height, int pixelFormat, unsigned char **jpegBuf, size_t *jpegSize);
functions.description: Compress a 13–16-bit-per-sample packed-pixel RGB/Gray/CMYK image into a lossless JPEG image with the same data precision.
requirements: Same structural requirements as tj3Compress8, but srcBuf is unsigned short* and precision set via TJPARAM_PRECISION (defaults to 16 if unset/out of range)
Lossless mode restrictions apply (see TJPARAM_LOSSLESS): no subsampling, no colorspace conversion, etc.
Returns 0 on success, -1 on error

functions.name: tj3CompressFromYUVPlanes8
functions.signature: DLLEXPORT int tj3CompressFromYUVPlanes8(tjhandle handle, const unsigned char * const *srcPlanes, int width, const int *strides, int height, unsigned char **jpegBuf, size_t *jpegSize);
functions.description: Compress separate 8-bit-per-sample Y, U(Cb), V(Cr) planes (or Y only for grayscale) into a lossy YCbCr or grayscale JPEG image.
requirements: handle must be initialized for compression
srcPlanes must provide pointers to required planes; plane sizes must match tj3YUVPlaneSize(...) for width/height/strides/subsampling (subsampling via TJPARAM_SUBSAMP)
width,height must be positive
If width/height not multiples of iMCU dimensions an intermediate copy will be performed
strides may be NULL (implies plane widths) or per-plane bytes/row; 0 value means plane width
jpegBuf/*jpegSize handling same as tj3Compress8
Returns 0 on success, -1 on error

functions.name: tj3CompressFromYUV8
functions.signature: DLLEXPORT int tj3CompressFromYUV8(tjhandle handle, const unsigned char *srcBuf, int width, int align, int height, unsigned char **jpegBuf, size_t *jpegSize);
functions.description: Compress an 8-bit-per-sample unified planar YUV buffer into a lossy YCbCr or grayscale JPEG image.
requirements: handle must be initialized for compression
srcBuf must be a unified YUV buffer sized per tj3YUVBufSize(width,align,height, subsamp via TJPARAM_SUBSAMP)
width,height positive; align must be power of 2
If width/height not multiples of iMCU dimensions an intermediate copy will be performed
jpegBuf/*jpegSize handling same as tj3Compress8
Returns 0 on success, -1 on error

functions.name: tj3EncodeYUVPlanes8
functions.signature: DLLEXPORT int tj3EncodeYUVPlanes8(tjhandle handle, const unsigned char *srcBuf, int width, int pitch, int height, int pixelFormat, unsigned char **dstPlanes, int *strides);
functions.description: Encode 8-bit packed RGB/Gray into separate 8-bit Y, U, V planes (color conversion + downsampling only; no JPEG entropy coding).
requirements: handle must be initialized for compression
srcBuf valid; width,height positive
pitch 0 implies width * tjPixelSize[pixelFormat]
pixelFormat must be valid TJPF
dstPlanes must point to plane pointers sized per tj3YUVPlaneSize for chosen subsampling (set via TJPARAM_SUBSAMP)
strides may be NULL (implies plane widths) or per-plane; 0 means plane width
Returns 0 on success, -1 on error

functions.name: tj3EncodeYUV8
functions.signature: DLLEXPORT int tj3EncodeYUV8(tjhandle handle, const unsigned char *srcBuf, int width, int pitch, int height, int pixelFormat, unsigned char *dstBuf, int align);
functions.description: Encode 8-bit packed RGB/Gray into unified planar YUV (color conversion + downsampling only).
requirements: handle must be initialized for compression
srcBuf valid; width,height positive
pitch 0 implies width * tjPixelSize[pixelFormat]
pixelFormat must be valid TJPF
dstBuf must be sized per tj3YUVBufSize(width, align, height, subsamp via TJPARAM_SUBSAMP)
align must be a power of 2; 1 = unpadded
Returns 0 on success, -1 on error

functions.name: tj3DecompressHeader
functions.signature: DLLEXPORT int tj3DecompressHeader(tjhandle handle, const unsigned char *jpegBuf, size_t jpegSize);
functions.description: Parse a JPEG image (or tables-only stream) and set instance parameters describing it; optionally extracts ICC profile if TJPARAM_SAVEMARKERS is 2 or 4.
requirements: handle must be initialized for decompression
jpegBuf must point to a complete JPEG or tables-only stream; jpegSize is its size in bytes (>0)
Returns 0 on success, -1 on error

functions.name: tj3GetICCProfile
functions.signature: DLLEXPORT int tj3GetICCProfile(tjhandle handle, unsigned char **iccBuf, size_t *iccSize);
functions.description: Retrieve ICC profile extracted by tj3DecompressHeader (when TJPARAM_SAVEMARKERS was 2 or 4). May allocate and return a buffer via iccBuf; size returned via iccSize.
requirements: handle must be initialized for decompression
iccSize must be non-NULL pointer to size_t
If iccBuf != NULL, on success it will be set to allocated buffer or NULL if none; free with tj3Free()
Once retrieved, the profile must be re-extracted before retrieving again
Returns 0 on success, -1 on error

functions.name: tj3GetScalingFactors
functions.signature: DLLEXPORT tjscalingfactor *tj3GetScalingFactors(int *numScalingFactors);
functions.description: Return a pointer to the list of decompression scaling factors supported; count returned via numScalingFactors.
requirements: numScalingFactors must be a valid pointer
Returns NULL on error (check tj3GetErrorStr)
Returned pointer is library-managed; treat as read-only

functions.name: tj3SetScalingFactor
functions.signature: DLLEXPORT int tj3SetScalingFactor(tjhandle handle, tjscalingfactor scalingFactor);
functions.description: Set the scaling factor for subsequent lossy decompression. Use TJUNSCALED for no scaling. Ignored for lossless JPEGs.
requirements: handle must be initialized for decompression
scalingFactor must be one of the supported factors from tj3GetScalingFactors() or TJUNSCALED
Scaling affects destination sizes; for YUV outputs, non-multiple-of-iMCU causes intermediate copy
Returns 0 on success, -1 on error

functions.name: tj3SetCroppingRegion
functions.signature: DLLEXPORT int tj3SetCroppingRegion(tjhandle handle, tjregion croppingRegion);
functions.description: Specify a cropping region for partial decompression of a lossy JPEG into a packed-pixel image.
requirements: handle must be initialized for decompression
Must call tj3DecompressHeader() prior to setting non-TJUNCROPPED region
croppingRegion.x must be evenly divisible by scaled iMCU width (TJSCALED(tjMCUWidth[subsamp], scalingFactor))
croppingRegion is specified relative to scaled dimensions
Returns 0 on success, -1 on error

functions.name: tj3Decompress8
functions.signature: DLLEXPORT int tj3Decompress8(tjhandle handle, const unsigned char *jpegBuf, size_t jpegSize, unsigned char *dstBuf, int pitch, int pixelFormat);
functions.description: Decompress a JPEG (2–8 bits/sample) into an 8-bit packed-pixel RGB/Gray/CMYK image with same data precision; sets describing parameters on return.
requirements: handle must be initialized for decompression
jpegBuf/jpegSize must specify the JPEG image
dstBuf must be large enough for pitch * destinationHeight samples (or region)
pitch 0 implies destinationWidth * tjPixelSize[pixelFormat]
pixelFormat must be a valid TJPF value
destinationWidth/Height depend on scaling and cropping for lossy JPEGs; equal to JPEG dimensions for lossless
Returns 0 on success, -1 on error

functions.name: tj3Decompress12
functions.signature: DLLEXPORT int tj3Decompress12(tjhandle handle, const unsigned char *jpegBuf, size_t jpegSize, short *dstBuf, int pitch, int pixelFormat);
functions.description: Decompress a JPEG (9–12 bits/sample) into a packed-pixel image of same precision.
requirements: Same structural requirements as tj3Decompress8; dstBuf is short*
Returns 0 on success, -1 on error

functions.name: tj3Decompress16
functions.signature: DLLEXPORT int tj3Decompress16(tjhandle handle, const unsigned char *jpegBuf, size_t jpegSize, unsigned short *dstBuf, int pitch, int pixelFormat);
functions.description: Decompress a lossless JPEG (13–16 bits/sample) into a packed-pixel image of same precision.
requirements: Same structural requirements as tj3Decompress8; dstBuf is unsigned short*
Returns 0 on success, -1 on error

functions.name: tj3DecompressToYUVPlanes8
functions.signature: DLLEXPORT int tj3DecompressToYUVPlanes8(tjhandle handle, const unsigned char *jpegBuf, size_t jpegSize, unsigned char **dstPlanes, int *strides);
functions.description: Decompress an 8-bit lossy JPEG into separate 8-bit Y, U, V planes (no color conversion to RGB).
requirements: handle must be initialized for decompression
jpegBuf/jpegSize specify JPEG
dstPlanes must reference buffers sized via tj3YUVPlaneSize for scaled JPEG dimensions (consider scaling factor) and subsampling reported by TJPARAM_SUBSAMP
strides may be NULL (implies scaled plane widths) or per-plane; 0 means scaled plane width
Returns 0 on success, -1 on error

functions.name: tj3DecompressToYUV8
functions.signature: DLLEXPORT int tj3DecompressToYUV8(tjhandle handle, const unsigned char *jpegBuf, size_t jpegSize, unsigned char *dstBuf, int align);
functions.description: Decompress an 8-bit lossy JPEG into a unified 8-bit planar YUV buffer.
requirements: handle must be initialized for decompression
jpegBuf/jpegSize specify JPEG
dstBuf must be sized via tj3YUVBufSize(scaledWidth, align, scaledHeight, subsamp)
align must be a power of 2
Returns 0 on success, -1 on error

functions.name: tj3DecodeYUVPlanes8
functions.signature: DLLEXPORT int tj3DecodeYUVPlanes8(tjhandle handle, const unsigned char * const *srcPlanes, const int *strides, unsigned char *dstBuf, int width, int pitch, int height, int pixelFormat);
functions.description: Convert separate 8-bit Y, U, V planes into an 8-bit packed RGB/Gray image (color conversion only).
requirements: handle must be initialized for decompression
srcPlanes must point to valid planes sized via tj3YUVPlaneSize for width/height/strides/subsamp (TJPARAM_SUBSAMP)
strides may be NULL (implies plane widths) or per-plane; 0 means plane width
dstBuf must be large enough for pitch*height bytes
pitch 0 implies width * tjPixelSize[pixelFormat]
pixelFormat must be valid TJPF
Returns 0 on success, -1 on error

functions.name: tj3DecodeYUV8
functions.signature: DLLEXPORT int tj3DecodeYUV8(tjhandle handle, const unsigned char *srcBuf, int align, unsigned char *dstBuf, int width, int pitch, int height, int pixelFormat);
functions.description: Convert a unified 8-bit planar YUV buffer into an 8-bit packed RGB/Gray image (color conversion only).
requirements: handle must be initialized for decompression
srcBuf must be a unified YUV buffer sized per tj3YUVBufSize(width, align, height, subsamp via TJPARAM_SUBSAMP)
align must be a power of 2
dstBuf must be large enough for pitch*height
pitch 0 implies width * tjPixelSize[pixelFormat]
pixelFormat must be valid TJPF
Returns 0 on success, -1 on error

functions.name: tj3TransformBufSize
functions.signature: DLLEXPORT size_t tj3TransformBufSize(tjhandle handle, const tjtransform *transform);
functions.description: Return the maximum buffer size (bytes) required for the destination JPEG when applying a given lossless transform/cropping (accounts for geometry, subsampling changes, grayscale, and any ICC profile from instance or source). Requires header to be read first.
requirements: handle must be initialized for transform
Must call tj3DecompressHeader() before calling this
transform must point to a valid tjtransform defining op/options/region
Returns 0 on error

functions.name: tj3Transform
functions.signature: DLLEXPORT int tj3Transform(tjhandle handle, const unsigned char *jpegBuf, size_t jpegSize, int n, unsigned char **dstBufs, size_t *dstSizes, const tjtransform *transforms);
functions.description: Perform up to n lossless transforms of a JPEG into n destination JPEGs using per-destination tjtransform settings (crop, rotate/flip, grayscale, markers, etc.).
requirements: handle must be initialized for transform
jpegBuf/jpegSize specify the source JPEG
n must be >= 1; arrays dstBufs, dstSizes, transforms must have length n
dstBufs[i] may be NULL (library allocates) or pre-allocated; unless TJPARAM_NOREALLOC, buffers may be reallocated and pointers updated
If pre-allocating, dstSizes[i] must be set to buffer size; upon return contains actual size
For cropping, constraints on r.x and r.y divisibility by iMCU sizes apply (see tjMCUWidth/Height); TJXOPT_PERFECT, TRIM, etc. affect behavior
Large embedded Exif may exceed worst-case; avoid TJPARAM_NOREALLOC or drop markers via TJXOPT_COPYNONE/TJPARAM_SAVEMARKERS
Returns 0 on success, -1 on error

functions.name: tj3LoadImage8
functions.signature: DLLEXPORT unsigned char *tj3LoadImage8(tjhandle handle, const char *filename, int *width, int align, int *height, int *pixelFormat);
functions.description: Load a packed-pixel image (BMP 8-bit or PBMPLUS PPM/PGM 2–8 bits/sample) into memory with specified row alignment and pixel format.
requirements: handle must be a valid instance
filename must reference an existing BMP/PPM/PGM file
width and height must be valid pointers to receive dimensions
align must be a power of 2 (row alignment in samples)
pixelFormat must be a valid pointer; pass TJPF_UNKNOWN to auto-select optimal; TJPF_GRAY restricts to PGM/grayscale BMP; TJPF_CMYK uses a simplistic conversion (testing only)
On success returns newly-allocated buffer; free with tj3Free()
Returns NULL on error

functions.name: tj3LoadImage12
functions.signature: DLLEXPORT short *tj3LoadImage12(tjhandle handle, const char *filename, int *width, int align, int *height, int *pixelFormat);
functions.description: Load a packed-pixel PBMPLUS (PPM/PGM) image into memory with 9–12 bits/sample precision, aligned and formatted as requested.
requirements: Same structural requirements as tj3LoadImage8; buffer element type is short
TJPF_GRAY only supports PGM; TJPF_UNKNOWN auto-selects; TJPF_CMYK uses simplistic conversion
Precision target set via TJPARAM_PRECISION (defaults to 12); up/down-conversion performed if needed
Free with tj3Free()

functions.name: tj3LoadImage16
functions.signature: DLLEXPORT unsigned short *tj3LoadImage16(tjhandle handle, const char *filename, int *width, int align, int *height, int *pixelFormat);
functions.description: Load a packed-pixel PBMPLUS (PPM/PGM) image into memory with 13–16 bits/sample precision, aligned and formatted as requested.
requirements: Same structural requirements as tj3LoadImage8; buffer element type is unsigned short
TJPF_GRAY only supports PGM; TJPF_UNKNOWN auto-selects; TJPF_CMYK uses simplistic conversion
Precision target via TJPARAM_PRECISION (defaults to 16); up/down-conversion performed if needed
Free with tj3Free()

functions.name: tj3SaveImage8
functions.signature: DLLEXPORT int tj3SaveImage8(tjhandle handle, const char *filename, const unsigned char *buffer, int width, int pitch, int height, int pixelFormat);
functions.description: Save a packed-pixel 2–8 bits/sample image buffer to disk (BMP for 8-bit or PBMPLUS PPM/PGM depending on extension).
requirements: handle must be a valid instance
filename specifies output path and determines format by extension (BMP/PPM/PGM); BMP requires 8-bit precision
buffer must point to image data with specified width/height/pitch
pitch 0 implies width * tjPixelSize[pixelFormat]
pixelFormat must be valid; TJPF_GRAY writes PGM or 8bpp BMP; TJPF_CMYK converted to RGB with simplistic algorithm
Source precision via TJPARAM_PRECISION (defaults to 8)
Returns 0 on success, -1 on error

functions.name: tj3SaveImage12
functions.signature: DLLEXPORT int tj3SaveImage12(tjhandle handle, const char *filename, const short *buffer, int width, int pitch, int height, int pixelFormat);
functions.description: Save a packed-pixel 9–12 bits/sample image buffer to PBMPLUS (PPM/PGM).
requirements: Same structural requirements as tj3SaveImage8; buffer element type is short
TJPF_GRAY writes PGM; others write PPM; TJPF_CMYK uses simplistic conversion
Source precision via TJPARAM_PRECISION (defaults to 12)
Returns 0 on success, -1 on error

functions.name: tj3SaveImage16
functions.signature: DLLEXPORT int tj3SaveImage16(tjhandle handle, const char *filename, const unsigned short *buffer, int width, int pitch, int height, int pixelFormat);
functions.description: Save a packed-pixel 13–16 bits/sample image buffer to PBMPLUS (PPM/PGM).
requirements: Same structural requirements as tj3SaveImage8; buffer element type is unsigned short
TJPF_GRAY writes PGM; others write PPM; TJPF_CMYK uses simplistic conversion
Source precision via TJPARAM_PRECISION (defaults to 16)

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Target data type: null-terminated C string (char*). The fuzzer provides std::string
# whose c_str() will be used. We should generate bytes that, when interpreted as a
# string (without embedded NUL terminators), exercise interesting cases. The library
# will truncate to JMSG_STR_PARM_MAX (80) chars when copying. We therefore aim to
# produce lengths around 0, 1, near 79-81, with diverse character classes.
# The function generate(seed) returns a bytes object up to 4096 bytes that represents
# the initial buffer for FUZZ_PARAM_STR (and similar). No file I/O.

_MAX_LEN = 4096

_ASCII_PRINTABLE = ''.join(chr(c) for c in range(32, 127))  # space..~
_ASCII_WHITESPACE = "\t\n\r \v\f"
_PUNCT = string.punctuation
_HEX = '0123456789abcdefABCDEF'

# Some interesting message-like templates and payloads, including long sequences
# and multi-line text. No embedded NULs.
_TEMPLATES: List[str] = [
    "",  # empty
    "a",  # single char
    "%s",  # printf-like
    "%%%d %x %p ",
    "path:/usr/local/bin; env=PROD; key=%016x; id=%d\n",
    "Unicode-ish: café naïve 東京 — emoji? ",
    "JSON:{\"msg\":\"%s\",\"id\":%d,\"ok\":true}",
    "APP14 Adobe marker note ",
    "JFIF v1.02 density=%dx%d unit=%d ",
    "Huffman: lens=%s vals=%s ",
]

# Repetitive payloads to reach boundary lengths
_PAYLOADS: List[str] = [
    "A",
    "0",
    "x",
    "-",
    "_",
    "#",
    "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. ",
    "Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit. ",
    "HEX:" + ("deadbeef" * 4) + " ",
]

# Boundary-focused target lengths around JMSG_STR_PARM_MAX (80)
_BOUNDARY_LENS = [0, 1, 2, 3, 7, 15, 31, 63, 79, 80, 81, 160, 255, 512, 1024]


def _randstr(rng: random.Random, length: int) -> str:
    # Mix printable ASCII, whitespace, and some non-ASCII bytes encoded as UTF-8
    # Note: std::string can hold arbitrary bytes; however, we avoid NULs.
    pieces: List[str] = []
    while len(''.join(pieces)) < length:
        choice = rng.randint(0, 4)
        if choice == 0:
            # printable run
            run = ''.join(rng.choice(_ASCII_PRINTABLE) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 16)))
        elif choice == 1:
            # whitespace run
            run = ''.join(rng.choice(_ASCII_WHITESPACE) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 8)))
        elif choice == 2:
            # punctuation heavy
            run = ''.join(rng.choice(_PUNCT) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 12)))
        elif choice == 3:
            # hex-like pattern
            run = '0x' + ''.join(rng.choice(_HEX) for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 12)))
        else:
            # UTF-8 multi-byte sequences (avoid NUL); include common code points
            cps = [0x00E9, 0x00E1, 0x00F1, 0x2014, 0x2603, 0x03B1, 0x03C0, 0x0416, 0x65E5, 0x672C]
            run = ''.join(chr(rng.choice(cps)) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 6)))
        pieces.append(run)
    s = ''.join(pieces)
    return s[:length]


def _build_message(rng: random.Random, target_len: int) -> str:
    # Start from a template and fill with content to approach target length.
    tmpl = rng.choice(_TEMPLATES)
    # Fill placeholders with deterministic-looking numbers/strings
    nums = [rng.randint(-2**31, 2**31 - 1) for _ in range(3)]
    fill = tmpl.replace("%d", str(nums[0])).replace("%x", format(abs(nums[1]), 'x')).replace("%s", _randstr(rng, rng.randint(3, 20)))
    # Now pad with payloads to near target_len
    s = fill
    while len(s) < target_len:
        s += rng.choice(_PAYLOADS)
        if rng.random() < 0.2:
            s += _randstr(rng, rng.randint(1, 24))
    # Optionally insert newlines and long words
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        inserts = rng.randint(1, 4)
        for _ in range(inserts):
            pos = rng.randint(0, max(0, len(s) - 1))
            s = s[:pos] + "\n" + s[pos:]
    return s[:target_len]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Choose a boundary length with some bias toward 0..200 and around 80
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        target_len = rng.choice(_BOUNDARY_LENS)
    else:
        # random in range but avoid exceeding max
        target_len = rng.randint(0, min(1024, _MAX_LEN))
        # Nudge toward ~80 occasionally
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            target_len = max(0, int(rng.gauss(80, 30)))
            target_len = max(0, min(target_len, 1024))

    s = _build_message(rng, target_len)

    # Ensure no NULs; replace any accidental NUL with '\uFFFD'
    if '\x00' in s:
        s = s.replace('\x00', '\uFFFD')

    # Encode as UTF-8, but if size exceeds limit, truncate bytes (avoid splitting code point poorly acceptable for fuzz input)
    b = s.encode('utf-8', errors='replace')
    if len(b) > _MAX_LEN:
        b = b[:_MAX_LEN]
        # Avoid ending with a partial multi-byte? Since errors='replace', slices are fine.

    return b

# Data type: binary file data
# Targets:
# - jpeg_stdio_dest: opens a fuzz-provided filename for writing and sets it as JPEG destination.
#   The callee only needs the path to be writable; the file contents are produced later by the
#   library, so the initial buffer can be anything. However, providing a plausible JPEG header
#   can help subsequent consumers if they re-open the file.
# - tjSaveImage: saves an image to a path. The buffer here is the file that will be written by
#   the library. Providing a valid filename with different extensions (bmp/ppm/pgm) can steer
#   different code paths. The initial file payload itself is not read by the callee.
#
# Strategy:
# - Generate a short bytes payload (<= 4096) that can be used as initial contents for a file.
# - Prefer constructing a minimal, valid container header chosen from: BMP (DIB), PPM (P6),
#   PGM (P5), or a minimal JFIF JPEG header. This increases the chance that any code which
#   subsequently inspects the file (outside these stubs) finds something valid.
# - Randomize selection via seed. Keep sizes small and consistent.
#
# Minimal builders below generate syntactically valid, small files.

_MAX_SIZE = 4096

def _pad(b: bytes, total: int) -> bytes:
    if len(b) >= total:
        return b[:total]
    return b + b"\0" * (total - len(b))


def _build_bmp(width: int, height: int, bpp: int) -> bytes:
    # Minimal uncompressed BI_RGB BMP with 54-byte header + pixel data.
    # Rows are padded to 4-byte boundaries.
    # bpp: 24 or 32; use no color table.
    row_bytes = ((width * (bpp // 8) + 3) // 4) * 4
    pixel_data_size = row_bytes * height
    file_size = 14 + 40 + pixel_data_size
    bfType = b"BM"
    bfSize = file_size
    bfReserved1 = 0
    bfReserved2 = 0
    bfOffBits = 14 + 40
    file_header = struct.pack("<2sIHHI", bfType, bfSize, bfReserved1, bfReserved2, bfOffBits)
    biSize = 40
    biWidth = width
    biHeight = height
    biPlanes = 1
    biBitCount = bpp
    biCompression = 0  # BI_RGB
    biSizeImage = pixel_data_size
    biXPelsPerMeter = 2835
    biYPelsPerMeter = 2835
    biClrUsed = 0
    biClrImportant = 0
    info_header = struct.pack(
        "<IIIHHIIIIII",
        biSize,
        biWidth,
        biHeight,
        biPlanes,
        biBitCount,
        biCompression,
        biSizeImage,
        biXPelsPerMeter,
        biYPelsPerMeter,
        biClrUsed,
        biClrImportant,
    )
    # Simple gradient pixel data
    pixels = bytearray()
    for y in range(height):
        row = bytearray()
        for x in range(width):
            if bpp == 24:
                # B, G, R
                row += bytes(((x * 11) % 256, (y * 17) % 256, ((x + y) * 7) % 256))
            else:
                # 32bpp BGRA
                row += bytes(((x * 11) % 256, (y * 17) % 256, ((x + y) * 7) % 256, 255))
        # pad to 4-byte boundary
        while len(row) % 4 != 0:
            row += b"\0"
        pixels += row
    return file_header + info_header + bytes(pixels)


def _build_ppm(width: int, height: int) -> bytes:
    # Binary PPM (P6)
    header = f"P6\n{width} {height}\n255\n".encode("ascii")
    pixels = bytearray()
    for y in range(height):
        for x in range(width):
            pixels += bytes(((x * 31) % 256, (y * 63) % 256, ((x + y) * 17) % 256))
    return header + bytes(pixels)


def _build_pgm(width: int, height: int) -> bytes:
    # Binary PGM (P5)
    header = f"P5\n{width} {height}\n255\n".encode("ascii")
    pixels = bytearray()
    for y in range(height):
        for x in range(width):
            pixels.append(((x * 23 + y * 19) % 256))
    return header + bytes(pixels)


def _build_min_jpeg(width: int, height: int) -> bytes:
    # Construct a tiny baseline JFIF JPEG with a single gray 8x8 (or chosen) image.
    # This is a handcrafted minimal stream: SOI, JFIF APP0, DQT, SOF0, DHT (DC/AC), SOS, EOI.
    # The entropy-coded segment here is a minimal EOB-only scan (all zeros block).
    w = max(1, min(65500, width))
    h = max(1, min(65500, height))

    def be16(x: int) -> bytes:
        return struct.pack(">H", x)

    soi = b"\xFF\xD8"
    # APP0 JFIF
    app0 = b"\xFF\xE0" + be16(16) + b"JFIF\x00\x01\x01\x00\x00\x01\x00\x01\x00\x00"
    # DQT (table 0, 8-bit)
    qtbl = bytes([
        16, 11, 12, 14, 12, 10, 16, 14,
        13, 14, 18, 17, 16, 19, 24, 40,
        26, 24, 22, 22, 24, 49, 35, 37,
        29, 40, 58, 51, 61, 60, 57, 51,
        56, 55, 64, 72, 92, 78, 64, 68,
        87, 69, 55, 56, 80, 109, 81, 87,
        95, 98, 103, 104, 103, 62, 77, 113,
        121, 112, 100, 120, 92, 101, 103, 99,
    ])
    dqt = b"\xFF\xDB" + be16(67) + b"\x00" + qtbl
    # SOF0 (baseline, 1 component grayscale)
    sof0 = b"\xFF\xC0" + be16(8 + 3 * 1) + b"\x08" + be16(h) + be16(w) + b"\x01" + b"\x01\x11\x00"
    # DHTs: minimal DC and AC for luminance
    # Standard small DC table
    dht_dc = (
        b"\xFF\xC4" + be16(3 + 12) + b"\x00" +
        b"\x00\x01\x05\x01\x01\x01\x01\x01\x01\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00" +
        b"\x00\x01\x02\x03\x04\x05\x06\x07\x08\x09\x0A\x0B"
    )
    # Small AC table including EOB (0x00) and a few codes
    dht_ac = (
        b"\xFF\xC4" + be16(3 + 162) + b"\x10" +
        b"\x00\x02\x01\x03\x03\x02\x04\x03\x05\x05\x04\x04\x00\x00\x01\x7D" +
        bytes(range(1, 0xB0))[:162]  # fill with sequential symbols to satisfy length
    )
    # SOS: single component, selectors 0 (DC), 0 (AC)
    sos = b"\xFF\xDA" + be16(6 + 2 * 1 + 3) + b"\x01\x01\x00\x00\x3F\x00"
    # Entropy-coded data: a single EOB (0x00) with byte-stuffing safeguards, then EOI
    # Use an empty block by emitting just 0x00 which should map to EOB in the chosen table.
    entropy = b"\x00"
    eoi = b"\xFF\xD9"
    return soi + app0 + dqt + sof0 + dht_dc + dht_ac + sos + entropy + eoi


def _pick_dims(rng: random.Random, max_side: int = 16) -> (int, int):
    w = rng.randint(1, max_side)
    h = rng.randint(1, max_side)
    return w, h


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    choice = rng.choice(["bmp24", "bmp32", "ppm", "pgm", "jpeg"])  # extensions targeted by tjSaveImage
    w, h = _pick_dims(rng, 16)

    if choice == "bmp24":
        data = _build_bmp(w, h, 24)
    elif choice == "bmp32":
        data = _build_bmp(w, h, 32)
    elif choice == "ppm":
        data = _build_ppm(w, h)
    elif choice == "pgm":
        data = _build_pgm(w, h)
    else:
        # minimal grayscale JPEG
        data = _build_min_jpeg(w, h)

    # Constrain size and ensure non-empty
    if not data:
        data = b"\0"
    if len(data) > _MAX_SIZE:
        # For oversized BMP/PPM/PGM, trim to max while keeping header intact
        # Heuristic: keep first 1024 bytes and last up to 1024 bytes if needed
        head = data[:1024]
        tail = data[-(max(0, _MAX_SIZE - len(head))):] if len(head) < _MAX_SIZE else b""
        data = (head + tail)[:_MAX_SIZE]
    return data
